pictures.scene: John Constable, The Hay Wain — the old cottage standing under its great tree beside the river where the same family has lived and worked for years, a prayer of Moses the man of God, Lord, You have been our dwelling place
pictures.name: pd_constable_woning

pictures.scene: Caspar Wolf, Lauteraar — the bare rock ledge over the glacier with two small figures standing on it under mountains older than any of them, through all generations, before the mountains were born
pictures.name: pd_wolf_bergen

pictures.scene: Isaac Levitan, Above Eternal Peace — the little wooden chapel on its headland under an enormous sky of moving cloud and water, or You brought forth the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting
pictures.name: pd_levitan_eeuwig

pictures.scene: Gustave Courbet, A Burial at Ornans — the crucifix raised over the open grave with the priest and the acolytes standing round it, You are God, You return man to dust
pictures.name: pd_courbet_stof

pictures.scene: Hubert Robert, Washerwomen in the Ruins of the Colosseum — women and children at their small fire under a vault that took an empire to build and has outlived it, return, O sons of mortals, for in Your sight a thousand years
pictures.name: pd_robert_duizend

pictures.scene: Joseph Wright of Derby, A Lake by Moonlight — the full moon laying its road across still water with one man walking the bank in the dark, are but a day that passes, or a watch of the night
pictures.name: pd_wright_nachtwake

pictures.scene: Ivan Shishkin, Midday near Moscow — the enormous sky standing over the ripe grain with the rutted road running away toward a far church, You sweep them away in their sleep, they are like the new grass of the morning
pictures.name: pd_shishkin_gras

pictures.scene: Ambrosius Bosschaert the Elder, Flower Still Life — the basket heaped with flowers at their fullest and one cut rose already lying spent on the stone ledge beside it, in the morning it springs up new, but by evening it fades and withers
pictures.name: pd_bosschaert_verwelkt

pictures.scene: Claude-Joseph Vernet, A Shipwreck in Stormy Seas — the dismasted ship going down under a black sky split by lightning while the survivors cling to the rocks, for we are consumed by Your anger and terrified by Your wrath
pictures.name: pd_vernet_toorn

pictures.scene: Hieronymus Bosch, The Seven Deadly Sins and the Four Last Things — the eye of God opened in the middle of the wheel with the warning written in it that God sees, You have set our iniquities before You, our secret sins in the light of Your presence
pictures.name: pd_bosch_zonden

pictures.scene: Ferdinand Hodler, Die Lebensmüden — the old men sitting bowed in a row with their hands folded and nothing left to say, for all our days decline in Your fury, we finish our years with a sigh
pictures.name: pd_hodler_zucht

pictures.scene: Titian, Allegory of Prudence — the three faces of one life set side by side, the young man, the man in his strength, and the old man already turning away, the length of our days is seventy years, or eighty if we are strong
pictures.name: pd_titiaan_zeventig

pictures.scene: Józef Chełmoński, Bociany — the old man and the boy in the flowering meadow looking up at the storks going over them and away, yet their pride is but labor and sorrow, for they quickly pass, and we fly away
pictures.name: pd_chelmonski_vliegen

pictures.scene: Georges Michel, L'Orage sur la vallée de la Seine — the torn storm sky coming down over the whole valley with the windmill small underneath it, who knows the power of Your anger, Your wrath matches the fear You are due
pictures.name: pd_michel_kracht

pictures.scene: Henry Ossawa Tanner, Nicodemus Visiting Jesus — the teacher and the old man sitting together on the moonlit roof over Jerusalem with the whole night to talk in, so teach us to number our days, that we may present a heart of wisdom
pictures.name: pd_tanner_tellen

pictures.scene: Gebhard Fugel, An den Wassern Babylons — the exiles sitting down by the river with their heads in their hands and one old man lifting his face and his hand to ask how long, return, O LORD, how long will it be, have compassion on Your servants
pictures.name: pd_fugel_keerterug

pictures.scene: Adolph Tidemand and Hans Gude, Bridal Procession on the Hardangerfjord — the boat going over the bright water in the early light with the fiddler playing and the bride crowned among her people, satisfy us in the morning with Your loving devotion, that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days
pictures.name: pd_gude_morgen

pictures.scene: Ilya Repin, They Did Not Expect Him — the man home at last from his years away standing in the doorway while his mother rises from her chair to him, make us glad for as many days as You have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen evil
pictures.name: pd_repin_blij

pictures.scene: Albert Anker, Die Dorfschule von 1848 — the old schoolmaster with his pointer on the open book and the whole bench of children leaning in to see it, may Your work be shown to Your servants, and Your splendor to their children
pictures.name: pd_anker_kinderen

pictures.scene: Léon Augustin Lhermitte, La Paye des moissonneurs — the reaper resting with his scythe and the coins being counted out into the hands that cut the harvest, may the favor of the Lord our God rest upon us, establish for us the work of our hands
pictures.name: pd_lhermitte_gunst

pictures.scene: Adolph von Menzel, Das Eisenwalzwerk — the men bearing down together with their tongs on the white-hot iron in the roar of the mill, yes, establish the work of our hands
pictures.name: pd_menzel_handen

lines.text: A prayer of Moses the man of God.
Lord, You have been our dwelling place
through all generations.
Before the mountains were born
or You brought forth the earth and the world,
from everlasting to everlasting
You are God.
You return man to dust,
saying, “Return, O sons of mortals.”
For in Your sight a thousand years
are but a day that passes,
or a watch of the night.
You sweep them away in their sleep;
they are like the new grass of the morning—
in the morning it springs up new,
but by evening it fades and withers.
For we are consumed by Your anger
and terrified by Your wrath.
You have set our iniquities before You,
our secret sins in the light of Your presence.
For all our days decline in Your fury;
we finish our years with a sigh.
The length of our days is seventy years—
or eighty if we are strong—
yet their pride is but labor and sorrow,
for they quickly pass, and we fly away.
Who knows the power of Your anger?
Your wrath matches the fear You are due.
So teach us to number our days,
that we may present a heart of wisdom.
Return, O LORD! How long will it be?
Have compassion on Your servants.
Satisfy us in the morning with Your loving devotion,
that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days.
Make us glad for as many days as You have afflicted us,
for as many years as we have seen evil.
May Your work be shown to Your servants,
and Your splendor to their children.
May the favor of the Lord our God rest upon us;
establish for us the work of our hands—
yes, establish the work of our hands!
